Summary
The southeastern escarpment of the Blue Rulge Mountains is occupied by three species of Plethodon. P. cinereus is found at elevations alove 3000 (eet, while P. glutinosus and P. jordani range over the entire escarpment. The downward extension of pardum to elevations below 1000 feet is probably the result of high rainfall at low elevations.
P. glutinosus and P. jordani differ in coloration and size at most escarpment localities. The latter shows great variation in iridophore pigmentation. L'opulations with a high incidence of brassy fleeking and white spotting occur on the southern edge of the Blue Ridge, while to the north a reduction in irrdophores_ is found. On the basis of clinal variation in pigmentation, recognition of the subspecies elemsonae and melaventris is no longer war-Cranted.
